a2948.speaker: United Nations
a2948.speech: According to the United Nations, the armed conflict between the State of Palestine and Israel, which began in October 2023 in the Gaza Strip, has already caused more than 45,000 deaths.

a2948.speaker: Fayez Jawad, Ambassador of Palestine accredited to Mozambique
a2948.speech: In a brief contact with the press minutes after the end of the meeting, said it had been an advantageous meeting because there was mutual interest in further cementing the relations of cooperation and friendship between the two parliaments; said he had confirmed Mozambique's support for the peace process under way in the Gaza Strip. "We exchanged views on strengthening our cooperation, which Mozambique has already demonstrated to the Palestinian people, at a time when our people face harmful wars," he stated.

a3025.speaker: American Academy of Pediatrics (research)
a3025.speech: Research by the American Academy of Pediatrics shows that excessive screen use can weaken memory, concentration, and the ability to solve and cope with challenges.

a3085.speaker: Donald J. Trump, US President
a3085.speech: Presented on Monday a 20-point plan to restore peace in Gaza; according to Trump, the plan goes beyond the war in the Gaza Strip since he states that this proposal would lead to peace throughout the region, speaking even of an "eternal peace" and the elimination of any danger in the Middle East "forever."

a3085.speaker: Washington (US administration)
a3085.speech: Asserts that the 20-point plan unveiled Monday at the White House constitutes a major diplomatic advance.

a3085.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a3085.speech: Expressed his support for Trump's peace plan, stating that it would achieve his country's war objectives; described Trump as the "best friend Israel has ever had in the White House" and asserted that no one else rivals him ; "Israel will recover all the hostages, Hamas's military capabilities and political domination will be dismantled, and Gaza will be guaranteed never again to represent a threat to Israel."

a3085.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a3085.speech: Warned that if Hamas rejected the plan, or accepted it and then "did everything to thwart it," Israel would finish the job itself ; "It may be for better or for worse, but it will happen."

a3085.speaker: Official familiar with the negotiations (anonymous), speaking to Reuters
a3085.speech: Told Reuters that Hamas would study and respond to the American peace plan "in good faith."

a3085.speaker: Palestinian Authority (statement)
a3085.speech: Welcomed the "sincere and determined" efforts of the American president; in a statement, the Authority also expressed its confidence in its ability to find a "path to peace."

a3085.speaker: United Nations spokesperson
a3085.speech: "We welcome all mediation efforts and are ready to support them, including by providing humanitarian aid," a UN spokesperson said Monday evening in New York.

a3110.speaker: Rolf A. Olson, Chargé d’Affaires a.i., US Embassy in Ghana (press release)
a3110.speech: “The United States commends the presidential candidates for signing the 4th Presidential Elections Peace Pact and congratulates the National Peace Council and the Institute of Democratic Governance for their tireless stewardship of this important initiative.” ; “The will of the Ghanaian people must not be thwarted by the threat of violence before, during, or after the upcoming elections. The United States wishes Ghana a peaceful, transparent, and credible electoral process on December 7.”

a3110.speaker: Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, Vice-President of Ghana and New Patriotic Party (NPP) presidential candidate
a3110.speech: Reiterated his resolve to uphold Ghana’s laws and ensure peace, stating: “I wholeheartedly pledge my commitment to work within the rules and collaborate with all to ensure a peaceful election.”

a3110.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, former President and National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate
a3110.speech: Echoed this commitment, urging collaborative efforts to maintain stability: “Let us pledge to promote peace. Let us work together to create an environment that is conducive to free, fair, and peaceful elections.”

a3126.speaker: U.S. Government / United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a3126.speech: Announced a new agriculture portfolio to foster inclusive economic growth and strengthen food systems in Nampula and Zambezia provinces, as part of the U.S. Government’s global hunger and food security initiative, Feed the Future (FtF); the portfolio is valued at $170 million USD and will help Mozambique build food systems that are inclusive, resilient, and sustainable.

a3126.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a3126.speech: Announced the new portfolio in Nampula and, speaking at the Unilurio Business School, touted the impacts of U.S. Government agriculture investments: “These funds will go towards innovative agricultural programs benefiting women, youth, and vulnerable communities in the provinces of central and northern Mozambique. They will connect farmers with new technologies, practices, and services that will boost productivity, increase rural incomes, improve nutrition and food security, and build the agribusiness private sector.”

a3305.speaker: UN report, Trends in maternal mortality (WHO on behalf of the UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group)
a3305.speech: Shows a 40% global decline in maternal deaths between 2000 and 2023 - largely due to improved access to essential health services; reveals that the pace of improvement has slowed significantly since 2016, and that an estimated 260 000 women died in 2023 as a result of complications from pregnancy or childbirth - roughly equivalent to one maternal death every two minutes ; provides the first global account of the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on maternal survival, with an estimated 40 000 more women dying in 2021 due to pregnancy or childbirth, increasing to 322 000 from 282 000 the previous year ; highlights persistent inequalities between regions and countries, with sub-Saharan Africa still accounting for approximately 70% of the global burden of maternal deaths in 2023, and nearly two-thirds of global maternal deaths now occurring in countries affected by fragility or conflict, where a 15-year-old girl faces a 1 in 51 risk of dying from a maternal cause compared to 1 in 593 in more stable countries.

a3305.speaker: United Nations (UN) agencies
a3305.speech: Highlight the threat of major backsliding as unprecedented aid cuts take effect around the world; warn that without urgent action pregnant women in multiple countries will face severe repercussions - particularly those in humanitarian settings where maternal deaths are already alarmingly high.

a3305.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a3305.speech: "While this report shows glimmers of hope, the data also highlights how dangerous pregnancy still is in much of the world today despite the fact that solutions exist to prevent and treat the complications that cause the vast majority of maternal deaths." ; "In addition to ensuring access to quality maternity care, it will be critical to strengthen the underlying health and reproductive rights of women and girls - factors that underpin their prospects of healthy outcomes during pregnancy and beyond."

a3305.speaker: Catherine Russell, UNICEF Executive Director
a3305.speech: "When a mother dies in pregnancy or childbirth, her baby's life is also at risk. Too often, both are lost to causes we know how to prevent." ; "Global funding cuts to health services are putting more pregnant women at risk, especially in the most fragile settings, by limiting their access to essential care during pregnancy and the support they need when giving birth. The world must urgently invest in midwives, nurses, and community health workers to ensure every mother and baby has a chance to survive and thrive."

a3305.speaker: Dr Natalia Kanem, UNFPA's Executive Director
a3305.speech: "Access to quality maternal health services is a right, not a privilege, and we all share the urgent responsibility to build well-resourced health systems that safeguard the life of every pregnant woman and newborn." ; "By boosting supply chains, the midwifery workforce, and the disaggregated data needed to pinpoint those most at risk, we can and must end the tragedy of preventable maternal deaths and their enormous toll on families and societies."

a3623.speaker: Ethiopia Humanitarian Response Plan for 2019 (launched by the National Disaster Risk Management Commission and UNOCHA)
a3623.speech: According to the plan, meeting the humanitarian need of 8.3 million people will cost 1.3 billion dollars; the budget has been lowered by almost a quarter from the previous year, and the current plan calls for 60pc of the budget to be covered by the Ethiopian government and 22pc by the World Food Program (WFP).

a3623.speaker: Debebe Zewde, director of public relations at the National Disaster Risk Management Commission
a3623.speech: Said of the humanitarian response plan budget: “The rest will be covered by the international community.”

a3623.speaker: Debebe Zewde, director of public relations at the National Disaster Risk Management Commission
a3623.speech: Said: “The government is working on returning displaced people to their homes by ensuring their safety and security, providing platforms for people-to-people reconciliation and the necessary aid. This will continue until the affected can get back up on their feet.”

a3623.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a3623.speech: According to sources close to the matter, around 600,000 people are still displaced from the Gedeo and Guji zones, where over a million people were displaced in April and June of 2018.

a3623.speaker: Adane Tesfaye (PhD), director of the Institute of Disaster Risk Management & Food Security Studies at Bahir Dar University
a3623.speech: Said that although preliminary studies have been done to assess the basic needs of the displaced people, a more thorough assessment needs to be done to properly identify what people in different parts of the country need: “A thorough damage, loss and need assessment needs to be conducted so that the developmental support will not mismatch the need of a particular area. But while this survey is being done, the government should keep providing basic support to the affected areas.” ; Added that communication between the public and agricultural, health and meteorological institutions and security forces needs to be improved so that such natural and human-made disasters can be better dealt with in the future.

a3659.speaker: Jerolinmek Matthew Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a3659.speech: Recounted the recent participation of Liberia's delegation, led by the Minister of Finance and Development Planning, at the Spring Meetings of the World Bank in Washington, D.C., saying the mission was strategic and aimed at securing partnerships and funding: "The Finance Minister informed us that based on the engagements during the Spring Meetings, we can expect significant progress in our national infrastructure programs," noting this includes developments in roads, energy, ports, and structures in both the health and education sectors ; on the long-stalled Lofa road project: "With the commitments secured, we can now assure the people of Lofa County that this government will deliver a paved road to their region before the end of its tenure."

a3659.speaker: Jerolinmek Matthew Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a3659.speech: Highlighted Liberia's growing international recognition and the push to secure a seat as a Non-Permanent Member of the United Nations Security Council: "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs provided a detailed briefing to the cabinet on how Liberia's repositioning on the global stage is taking shape. Based on all calculations and efforts so far, the country is on the verge of being elected to serve on the UN Security Council," ; expressed satisfaction over Liberia's expanding bilateral and multilateral relationships, noting that the country's foreign engagements have sparked increased international interest and support.

a3659.speaker: Jerolinmek Matthew Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a3659.speech: Described the presentation and endorsement of a new Domestic Resource Mobilization Strategy developed by the Liberia Revenue Authority as one of the most important discussions at the recent cabinet meeting, explaining that the strategy aims to reduce Liberia's dependency on foreign aid and increase internal capacity to fund development: "Yes, partners are helping us, but we've seen the risks of overreliance," citing the scaling back of U.S. support through USAID as a wake-up call ; "This strategy provides a pathway for Liberia to generate up to 1.5 billion U.S. dollars in national revenue, which would empower the government to better fund hospitals, schools, and other critical social services." ; described the five-year implementation cost of $36.53 million as both logical and necessary.

a3659.speaker: Jerolinmek Matthew Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a3659.speech: Disclosed that ministers and heads of agencies are now required to sign performance management contracts, a move designed to hold public servants accountable for the delivery of services: "No longer will individuals operate solely based on the act that established their institution. Under the Boakai administration, we are demanding results."

a3659.speaker: Jerolinmek Matthew Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a3659.speech: Revealed that the cabinet has endorsed a new concept for the Presidential Delivery Unit (PDU), emphasized the need for a strong PDU to support presidential oversight, and explained that the previous administration rendered the PDU dormant, using it instead as a placement center for political appointees: "Minister Bility undertook a study tour in South Africa, which culminated in a new policy concept that has now been endorsed by the cabinet. We look forward to a robust and functional PDU that aligns with the government's development agenda."

a3659.speaker: Director General of the Cabinet of Liberia
a3659.speech: Presented updates on the Performance Management Compliance System, outlining a two-phase approach: phase one, already completed, included the development and publication of service delivery charters and the strengthening of internal controls; phase two will require each institution to develop a strategic plan, implement service standards, identify resource leakages, improve internal resource mobilization, and build institutional capacity.

a3723.speaker: Ministry of Trade & Regional Integration (MoTRI), under Gebremeskel Chala (directive)
a3723.speech: Imposed a new directive on exporters requiring that they must now align their international sale prices with or surpass those set on the Ethiopian Commodity Exchange (ECX) floor.

a3723.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato, economist
a3723.speech: Argues for a substantial role of the state in galvanising economic growth while safeguarding capitalism from its inherent vices (the “Entrepreneurial State” concept).

a3723.speaker: International Debt Report
a3723.speech: As outlined in the report, Ethiopia’s external debt stock escalated almost threefold in a decade to 27.7 billion dollars by mid-last year, part of a broader trend where the escalating debt burden reached 1.1 trillion dollars across low- and middle-income countries, raising alarm over debt sustainability and servicing capabilities.

a3723.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3723.speech: The Fund’s insistence on a raft of policy reforms — including liberalising the foreign exchange market, budgetary discipline, and curtailment of off-budget expenditures — demonstrates the imperative of adopting stringent measures to restore macroeconomic equilibrium.

a4119.speaker: Alousseni Sanou, Malian Minister of Economy and Finance
a4119.speech: assured that the tariff would have no negative impact on prices for consumers: “It is rather a redistribution of the existing ECOWAS tax, so that the cost of imported food products will remain stable.”

a4157.speaker: Yenataban Koné, Director of Technologies and Information Systems at the Ivorian Ministry of Education
a4157.speech: Said this integrated tool will make it possible to considerably reduce administrative red tape and to improve coordination between the various services of the education system: “The SIGE will simplify and optimise administrative, pedagogical and logistical operations, facilitate the smooth circulation of information, strengthen resource planning, the monitoring of education policies and their evaluation.”

a4157.speaker: Mariatou Koné, Ivorian Minister of National Education
a4157.speech: In her speech, stressed the importance of having reliable education data in real time for better planning and effective steering of the sector: “Thanks to the SIGE, the ministry will be able to rigorously monitor the schooling of children across the whole territory, plan the construction of school infrastructure, allocate human and material resources in an equitable and efficient manner, combat school drop-out and strengthen accountability towards citizens and partners.” ; Issued an appeal to financial, bilateral and multilateral partners and to the private sector to support the large-scale deployment of the tool: “The success of this roll-out will require substantial technical and human resources, as well as strategic support to guarantee the alignment of the SIGE with national education priorities and international standards.”

a4157.speaker: Jessica Davis Ba, Ambassador of the United States to Côte d’Ivoire
a4157.speech: Hailed the Minister’s leadership and recalled the shared vision behind this project: “The SIGE embodies a quality education, supported by modern, efficient and human-centred tools.”

a4174.speaker: Filimão Suaze, spokesperson of the Mozambican Council of Ministers and Deputy Minister of Justice, Constitutional and Religious Affairs
a4174.speech: Explained that the measure aims to clarify ADIN's duties and powers with regard to institutional coordination and articulation ; said that with the amendment ADIN will now carry out the supervision and technical coordination of the implementation of all development programmes and projects of the sectors and partners, and will likewise “articulate the actors involved in the development of the northern region”.

a4302.speaker: Maazou Oumani, commercial director of SONIDEP (Niger's national petroleum products company)
a4302.speech: Said two main reasons explain the shortage: the removal of the fuel subsidy in Nigeria caused prices to soar there, making clandestine importation of Nigerian gasoline into Niger impossible; and for more than a year the efforts of the Defence and Security Forces have effectively stopped smuggling, which formerly represented 40 to 50% of national consumption ; “Today, all consumption rests on the official service stations.”

a4302.speaker: Maazou Oumani, commercial director of SONIDEP
a4302.speech: “We receive on average 25 tankers per day, whereas demand in the capital alone is 25 to 26 tankers, and that of the whole country between 40 and 50 tankers.”

a4302.speaker: Maazou Oumani, commercial director of SONIDEP
a4302.speech: Reassured Nigeriens by announcing the availability of considerable stocks in Lomé, Togo: “The trucks are on their way to ensure the country’s supply” ; “SONIDEP does indeed have stocks abroad that we are bringing in by every possible means.”

a4443.speaker: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport (South Korea)
a4443.speech: According to the Ministry, the Jeju Air Flight 2216, a Boeing 737-800, carrying 181 passengers and crew, collided with a flock of birds and crash-landed at Muan International Airport on Sunday morning, skidding along the runway on its belly before erupting into flames.

a4443.speaker: Initial reports (unattributed official accounts)
a4443.speech: Initial reports suggest the crash may have been caused by bird strikes, potentially exacerbated by a landing gear malfunction or poor weather conditions.

a4443.speaker: A father of one of the victims (unnamed)
a4443.speech: One father recounted how he had spoken to his daughter just days before the crash, never imagining it would be their last conversation.

a4443.speaker: Government of South Korea
a4443.speech: The government has pledged to conduct a thorough investigation while addressing the safety concerns highlighted by this disaster.

a4448.speaker: Martin Griffiths, head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4448.speech: Said that it "is cruel to see that in many humanitarian operations, aid agencies are getting by on very little financial means at the very moment when the needs of populations require them to step up their action. Thanks to the generosity of a wide range of donors, we can count on CERF to fill some of the gaps. Lives are thus saved. But we need individual donors to do the same - this is a fund by all and for all."

a4551.speaker: Li Yangchun, project director of the Odienne-Mali and Guinea Borders road (China Harbour Engineering Company)
a4551.speech: “This road is an essential access route for Mali and Guinea toward Ivorian ports” ; “The journey between Odienne, the district capital, and the Malian border has gone from 4 hours 30 to 1 hour 30, and from three hours to just one to reach the Guinean border. Transport efficiency has improved considerably.”

a4551.speaker: Yacouba Kone, 48, trader in cashew nuts and cement
a4551.speech: “Before 2020, it was extremely difficult for trucks to get here” ; said he had closely observed the changes over his twenty years of business: “Now trucks circulate freely, logistics are smooth. Just yesterday I unloaded two trucks without any problem.”

a4551.speaker: Aka Kanga, laboratory technician from a nearby village
a4551.speech: “There were no passable roads and the rugged terrain prevented villagers from transporting their harvests. A lot of cashew nuts rotted in the fields” ; “This road built by a Chinese company truly changes the lives of our population.”

a4551.speaker: Moussa Soumahoro, secretary to the village chief of Samatiguila, Kabadougou region
a4551.speech: “The road is the first development of a country.”

a4551.speaker: Adiarra Coulibaly, grocer established along the road
a4551.speech: “Life is much simpler now. With more customers and goods circulating without hindrance, my business is prospering” ; confided that her clientele now comes from across the region.

a4551.speaker: Arouna Diarrassouba, 36, cross-border trader
a4551.speech: “I trade in clothing, maize and shoes, mainly toward Manankoro, on the Malian border, sometimes even as far as Guinea” ; “Today travel is easier, transport is convenient and my business is doing better. I travel two to three times a week.”

a4551.speaker: Tian Lei, commercial director of the project (China Harbour Engineering Company)
a4551.speech: According to him, CHEC gave priority to local employment, generating more than 2,000 jobs during construction, and invested in skills transfer through the training of engineers and technicians.

a4551.speaker: Shi Tianhu, interpreter in charge of managing the local workforce (CHEC)
a4551.speech: “We always try to bring something where the road passes: digging wells, repairing village paths, offering school supplies” ; “We are proud to concretely improve the lives of the inhabitants.”

a4551.speaker: Niamien Assassy Caunan, head of the sub-prefecture of Tienko, Folon region
a4551.speech: “It is a remarkable project, beneficial both for the country and for the population” ; “It has truly connected our regions, boosted economic activity and considerably improved living conditions. Traffic has increased, trade is prospering, new dwellings are being built, the changes are real and visible.”

a4592.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a4592.speech: Alleged that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) has been funding terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram, and accused USAID during the inaugural hearing of the Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency (DOGE) of misappropriating taxpayers' funds, some of which he claimed ended up in the hands of terrorist organisations: "Who gets some of that money? Does that name ring a bell to anybody in the room? Because your money, your money - $697 million annually, plus shipments of cash - funds Madrasas, ISIS, Al-Qaeda, Boko Haram, ISIS-Khorasan, and terrorist training camps. That's what it's funding."

a4592.speaker: General Christopher Gwabin Musa, Nigeria's Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)
a4592.speech: Has repeatedly highlighted the role of external support in sustaining terrorist activities in the country, consistently questioning how terrorist groups in Nigeria manage to sustain their operations despite sustained military offensives, and pointing to foreign financial and logistical support as a critical factor; has alleged that some international organisations operating in conflict zones, particularly in the North-East, indirectly support terrorist groups through funding and training, thereby prolonging the insurgency ; revealed that many surrendered or captured Boko Haram fighters have been found in possession of foreign currency: "As we speak, over 120,000 Boko Haram members have surrendered, and most of them came with hard currency. How did they get it? How are they funded? How did they get the training? How did they get the equipment?" ; cited instances where some international NGOs, ostensibly providing humanitarian aid, paid up to ten years' rent in advance for properties in insurgency-prone areas, questioning whether these NGOs had foreknowledge that terrorism would persist for another decade ; emphasised that terrorism financing is the lifeblood of these groups and that cutting off their funding sources would naturally lead to their collapse, calling for a more proactive approach including enhanced financial intelligence and international cooperation.

a4592.speaker: General Christopher Gwabin Musa, Nigeria's Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)
a4592.speech: During an interview with Al Jazeera last month, urged the United Nations to investigate the funding and training of Boko Haram terrorists: "The UN needs to come in because we need to trace the funding. It is an international flow, and we do not have control over that."

a4592.speaker: Nigerian military high command
a4592.speech: Attributed the 2025 escalation in terrorist activities to the influx of foreign fighters from the Sahel region, alongside the activities of local collaborators who serve as informants for terrorist groups.

a4711.speaker: Malawi government
a4711.speech: Announced that it is implementing responsive measures to manage the impact of the recent decision by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) to halt its operations across the globe.

a4711.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Malawi government spokesperson
a4711.speech: Acknowledged the fears surrounding the foreign policy review but emphasized the need for countries to be economically independent to effectively navigate changes in foreign aid policy: "We cannot continue to rely heavily on donor aid," Kunkuyu said in an interview with MIJ Online. "We need to find ways to be self-sufficient and reduce our dependence on foreign aid." ; Emphasized that the government is committed to finding alternative solutions to mitigate the impact of USAID's decision: "We are working closely with other development partners to ensure that our development programs continue uninterrupted."

a4711.speaker: A development expert (unnamed)
a4711.speech: "It's high time that Malawi and other developing countries start to think about how they can reduce their dependence on foreign aid. The government's decision to implement responsive measures is a positive step towards achieving economic independence."

a4711.speaker: USAID (agency strategy document)
a4711.speech: USAID's own strategy emphasizes the importance of helping countries increase their commitment and build capacity to manage their own development challenges.

a4766.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4766.speech: Said the administration's aim was a program-by-program review of which projects make “America safer, stronger or more prosperous.” ; Said the decision to shut down U.S.-funded programs during the 90-day review meant the U.S. was “getting a lot more cooperation” from recipients of humanitarian, development and security assistance.

a4766.speaker: Marco Rubio, then Florida senator (2017 social media post)
a4766.speech: Said foreign assistance was “not charity,” that the U.S. “must make sure it is well spent” and called foreign aid “critical to our national security.”

a4766.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a4766.speech: Alleges USAID funding has been used to launch deadly programs and called it a “criminal organization.”

a4766.speaker: Elon Musk (post on X)
a4766.speech: “Live by executive order, die by executive order,” Musk said on X Saturday in reference to USAID.

a4766.speaker: Congressional Research Service (report published last month)
a4766.speech: The U.S. spent roughly $40 billion in foreign aid in the 2023 fiscal year, according to a report published last month by the nonpartisan Congressional Research Service.

a4766.speaker: AP-NORC poll (March 2023)
a4766.speech: About 6 in 10 U.S. adults said the U.S. government was spending “too much” overall on foreign aid; roughly 7 in 10 U.S. adults said the U.S. government was putting too much money toward assistance to other countries; about 9 in 10 Republicans and 55% of Democrats agreed that the country was overspending on foreign aid; about 6 in 10 U.S. adults said the government was spending “too little” on domestic issues.

a4766.speaker: Kaiser Family Foundation surveys
a4766.speech: Have found that on average, Americans say spending on foreign aid makes up 31% of the federal budget rather than closer to 1% or less.

a4766.speaker: Democrats
a4766.speech: Say presidents lack the constitutional authority to eliminate USAID.

a4766.speaker: Government Accountability Office (ruling)
a4766.speech: Later ruled that the use of freezes and other tactics to cut the flow of funds already appropriated by Congress violated a law known as the Impoundment Control Act.

a4894.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4894.speech: In late January, US President Donald Trump ordered a 90-day suspension of foreign aid, halting all financial assistance distributed by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

a4950.speaker: Organisers of the InnTech Summit 2025 (press statement)
a4950.speech: Said the event will focus on the theme "AI, Digital Economy, and Sustainability"; said the 2025 edition will drive cross-sector collaboration and dialogue around key priorities such as harnessing AI for economic diversification, building resilient digital economies, aligning innovation with environmental sustainability and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and strengthening Africa's competitiveness in the global digital ecosystem.

a4950.speaker: Engr. Ahmed Mansur, Chairman of the InnTech Summit
a4950.speech: Emphasised the event's significance, noting that Africa is on the verge of a new era driven by innovation and technology: "The InnTech Summit 2025 provides a strategic platform to align our digital transformation journey with sustainable economic growth."

a5094.speaker: West Africa Network for Peacebuilding (WANEP) and the National Peace Council (NPC)
a5094.speech: Have urged political parties to cooperate with the Electoral Commission (EC) and National Election Security Taskforce in the discharge of its duties: "We implore political parties to encourage their supporters to be law-abiding and all Ghanaians to be peaceful during the post-election period."

a5094.speaker: Rev. Dr Ernest Adu-Gyamfi, Chairman of the National Peace Council
a5094.speech: Said the National Election Taskforce "is encouraged to deploy timely and effective response mechanism to address security concerns in this post-election period" ; "With reference to the Election Peace Pact signed, we encourage all stakeholders to utilise laid-down procedures to seek redress on any electoral grievances." ; entreated Ghanaians to celebrate victory in magnanimity, demonstrate patriotism and embrace civic responsibility in the interest of social cohesion and national unity.

a5094.speaker: 2024 Election Situation Room (ESR)
a5094.speech: Encouraged all parties and supporters to remain calm and uphold the rule of law to preserve the peace of the country.

a5094.speaker: Rev. Dr Ernest Adu-Gyamfi, Chairman of the National Peace Council
a5094.speech: Commended Ghanaians for their patriotism and patience in the electoral process and applauded the efforts of the EC, political parties, the National Election Security Taskforce, civil society organisations, women, youth groups and the media for their contribution towards the relatively peaceful elections: "We commend Dr Mahamudu Bawumia for upholding his commitment to the Presidential Peace Pact in his concession speech this morning. This action has enhanced Ghana's democratic process and made our country proud and confirmed our position as the beacon of democracy in Africa." ; congratulated president-elect John Mahama for his social media acceptance of the concession by the NPP presidential candidate.

a5094.speaker: Rev. Dr Ernest Adu-Gyamfi, Chairman of the National Peace Council
a5094.speech: On lessons learnt from the election, said the signing of the presidential and parliamentary peace pacts was essential to committing political party candidates and their supporters to peaceful elections and acceptance of the outcomes: "Early concession of defeat by presidential and parliamentary candidates is vital to douse political tensions in the post-election period."

a5196.speaker: Dr Mohamed Diane, Director General of the Sino-Guinean Hospital (HASIGUI)
a5196.speech: Explained the procedures put in place to guarantee complete transparency in the management of patients: “There are visible price lists. At the Sino-Guinean hospital, everything is transparent. In the main hall of the principal building, you can see two large screens displaying the duty team each day, with their names, their photographs and their telephone numbers. The consultation team and all the doctors who are to see patients are also displayed automatically. At the Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital in Kipe, we have a single cash desk system. When I see you in consultation, I already have a receipt for the consultation. The tests prescribed are itemised with their specific costs. You then go to the cash desk, where the prices of services are clearly indicated. Likewise, at the pharmacy, a small ticket lists all the prices and the items available, thereby guaranteeing complete transparency.”

a5196.speaker: Dr Mohamed Diane, Director General of the Sino-Guinean Hospital (HASIGUI)
a5196.speech: On fees: “For consultations, the official fee is 50,000 francs. With the exception of emergency services, which are 60,000 francs. Specialist consultations for children cost 30,000 francs. This fee is paid only once a month. As regards surgical procedures, to date none exceeds 5 million francs. That amount includes everything: the pre-anaesthesia consultation, loco-regional or general anaesthesia, the surgical procedure itself, and the necessary consumables. However, there are items such as implants for neurosurgery or femurs and hips in traumatology which the hospital does not control, because they are not medical products available locally. In other health facilities in our country, you can be asked for 50 million or 90 million francs, on top of being made to buy the consumables separately. Here, the amount of 5 million includes everything, including the consumables.”

a5196.speaker: Dr Mohamed Diane, Director General of the Sino-Guinean Hospital (HASIGUI)
a5196.speech: Brandishing material evidence and precise data on cases of hospitalisation and death, vigorously rejected the allegations presenting his hospital as a “death house”, revealing that the hospital often receives bodies for various reasons, including deaths that occurred outside the establishment ; said a senior official of the country had asked him whether all the bodies registered at the morgue were really hospital patients, and that he cited examples such as the artist Mory Kante, the magistrate Doura Cherif and the former president of the National Assembly Aboubacar Sompare, none of whom died at the Sino-Guinean hospital ; explained that certain people are actively and maliciously engaged in spreading false information about the hospital to the population.

a5196.speaker: Dr Mohamed Diane, Director General of the Sino-Guinean Hospital (HASIGUI)
a5196.speech: Presented the hospital's monitoring data: “We have a total of 112 beds, of which 103 are open. The hospital's total staff to date is 164 people, all categories combined, with a male/female ratio of 1.56” ; “The epidemiological profile includes the main reasons for consultation. We compared the first half of 2023 with the first half of 2024 in order to assess our progress and our shortcomings. For example, consultations for 'other osteo-articular conditions' went from 242 in 2023 to 445 in 2024, which shows an increase in services. This increase goes hand in hand with the qualification and quality of the providers. We have also identified the main causes of hospitalisation... As regards the so-called 'tracer' pathologies, we have here five pathologies with their fatality rates” ; described the hospital's strategy for the management of deaths, distinguishing expected deaths (end-of-life patients, severe head trauma with a very low Glasgow score) from hospital deaths, for which “we have a procedure for examining what was done or omitted in the patient's treatment... in order to improve our practices and avoid similar incidents in the future”, with any serious condition lasting five days in a specialist service closely monitored and regular updates given to families.

a5220.speaker: Musa Salifu Taylor, Capacity Building Team Lead for the Feed the Future Market Systems and Resilience (MSR) Activity
a5220.speech: indicated that if businesses were not registered and formalised, it led to limited markets; stated that as part of the project, they thought it wise to begin the journey with the MSMEs by assisting them to register their businesses so that they would be able to improve them for their own benefit; charged them to build a mutually beneficial relationship with the Business Resource Centre (BRC) and other service providers to improve their firms.

a5220.speaker: Gifty Akapule, Women and Youth Entrepreneurship Specialist, Feed the Future Ghana MSR Activity
a5220.speech: said a needs assessment conducted on 241 MSMEs revealed that about 71 per cent operated informally without business certificates; stated that such a situation hindered the businesses from accessing huge markets to sustain their respective trades: “Through the project, we decided to formalise 300 MSMEs in the beneficiary regions for them to operate formally.” ; explained that one of the requirements for MSMEs to have access to credit facilities from financial institutions was a business certificate and proper record keeping: “We believe that the support provided to them will enable them to receive financial support to run their businesses.” ; implored the beneficiaries to properly manage their business for them to stand the test of time and to contribute to the growth and development of the informal sector in the country.

a5220.speaker: Ephrem Duorinaa, consultant to the project
a5220.speech: encouraged them to continue building upon what they had learned, to innovate and to collaborate with others to transform their trades; while commending USAID and its partners for the project, he called for continuous collaboration among stakeholders towards creating a future where every MSME had the opportunity to thrive.

a5220.speaker: Enoch Akortia, official at the Upper East Regional Office, Ghana Standards Authority
a5220.speech: urged them to act with integrity and contribute to the continued advancement of their respective businesses and contribute to the growth of the national economy.

a5314.speaker: Dr. David Moinina Sengeh, Chief Minister of Sierra Leone
a5314.speech: Highlighted the success of the Salone Civic Festival, an event that brought together citizens and government officials to discuss progress and challenges.

a5314.speaker: Dr. David Moinina Sengeh, Chief Minister of Sierra Leone
a5314.speech: Emphasized the government's efforts to attract foreign investment, citing significant investments from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) and other sources, and assured citizens that these funds, exceeding $1 billion and to be used to improve access to electricity, will be utilized effectively through implementing partners, ensuring transparency and accountability; he also pointed to other successful initiatives, such as the British investment in Miro at Mile 91, which has created numerous job opportunities for young people in the region, and to substantial funding from the U.S. Development Finance Corporation (DFC), which will directly benefit citizens through job creation during the implementation of electricity infrastructure projects.

a5314.speaker: Dr. David Moinina Sengeh, Chief Minister of Sierra Leone
a5314.speech: Emphasized that the government has made significant strides in stabilizing the economy, citing improvements in the exchange rate and increased revenue from the tourism sector following the completion of the new airport.

a5314.speaker: Dr. David Moinina Sengeh, Chief Minister of Sierra Leone
a5314.speech: Declared this year as "a year of delivery and bold action," and highlighted the government's commitment to building upon the successes of the past year and implementing policies that will further improve the lives of all Sierra Leoneans.

a5376.speaker: Rabisoni Chipangula, secretary of the Mbenje Island Committee and chairperson of Chikombe Beach Village Committee (BVC)
a5376.speech: Expressed frustration about the absence of toilets at the island, pointing out that Mbenje Island's needs have gone unheeded for nearly two decades. "It's almost 24 years now, since we started appealing for help for modern toilets, but the situation remains unchanged." ; "The island is rocky, making it difficult to dig latrines. We have approached partners like Ripple Africa, Usaid through the Refresh programme, and the Salima District Council for assistance, but there has been no response." ; "Just yesterday, health workers from Salima District Hospital visited to distribute mosquito nets, and they witnessed the poor state of sanitation on the island."

a5376.speaker: Willies Chanozga Mwandira, Wesnet executive director
a5376.speech: Says despite that Mbenje is rocky, there are some technologies such as using the same stones to build toilet facilities on top of the rocks not downwards; said all what is required is proper advice from the District Commissioner and the council can mobilise the service providers to go there and provide with the right directions in terms of how those people can have proper toilets; said communities at Mbenje can learn from some of the fishermen nearby in Nkhotakota District who have successfully generated revenue from toilet facilities which have been used to improve sanitation infrastructure.

a5376.speaker: Willies Chanozga Mwandira, Wesnet executive director
a5376.speech: Commented on the government of Malawi's plans to start pumping water from Lake Malawi and supply it to the City of Lilongwe through the Salima-Lilongwe water project: "That is a very important project for the country and as Malawians that is a resilient source of water. It can't be good to learn that some people who live at an island do not have toilets." ; "The imagination that would come is that our water in the lake will not be suitable for human consumption, it will be contaminated because of the fishermen in places like at Mbenje island." ; "I think it is important that we do something about it."

a5376.speaker: Amakhosi Jere, deputy country director for the Restoring Fisheries for Sustainable Livelihoods in Lake Malawi (Refresh) project funded by Usaid
a5376.speech: Explained that Salima District Council is the primary authority for addressing service delivery issues, including sanitation; noted that the Refresh project provided support in terms of training and capacity building, but the responsibility for building sanitation infrastructure lies with local authorities. "Salima District Council is best placed to comment on issues of service delivery." ; "We have helped to highlight the gaps, but the responsibility for addressing these issues falls to the local government."

a5376.speaker: Salima District Fisheries (office)
a5376.speech: Confirmed that Mbenje Island lacks toilet facilities, and also acknowledged that the community's request for help has been long ignored.

a5376.speaker: Patrick Zakeyo, district fisheries officer
a5376.speech: Said that while his office has raised concerns with the relevant authorities, they do not have the resources to construct toilets on the island; suggested that a self-financing model where local authorities collect fees from fishermen to fund the construction of toilets could be a possible solution.

a5376.speaker: The International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement 2024 statistics
a5376.speech: Says 3.5 billion people still live without access to safely managed sanitation and even more concerning, an estimated 419 million people still practice open defecation, which does not only increase the risk of infectious diseases, but also puts people, particularly women and children, in unsafe and vulnerable situations.

a5489.speaker: Janez Lenarcic, European Commissioner for Crisis Management
a5489.speech: "the Humanitarian Air Bridge to Mozambique ensured crucial assistance offered by Italy and Portugal to save the lives of people in Mozambique in a situation of vulnerability in Cabo Delgado, where the humanitarian situation continues to worsen. Humanitarian Air Bridge flights, which began in 2020 when transport and air traffic were restricted due to the coronavirus pandemic, are now activated in other challenging humanitarian environments. This is another example of Team Europe in action, a tangible example of European solidarity."

a5489.speaker: European Union
a5489.speech: Continues to advocate greater access for humanitarian personnel and assistance and the removal of obstacles delaying the delivery of aid to those who need it; calls for respect and compliance with international human rights standards and international humanitarian law.

a5489.speaker: Antonio Sanchez-Benedito Gaspar (@SBeneditoEU), EU official (Twitter post, July 9, 2021)
a5489.speech: "Third & final flight of the Humanitarian Air Bridge for #CaboDelgado arrived with humanitarian assistance, medical equipmt/hygiene kits/medicines for the population affected by violence. In total 20+ tons of humanitarian asssiatance thanks to IT PT @ECHO_CESAfrica efforts."

a5726.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the US Department of Government Efficiency
a5726.speech: Revealed/admitted that he was mistaken when he criticised the shipment of 50 million dollars' worth of condoms to the Gaza Strip, explaining that the condoms were sent to the province of Gaza in Mozambique for an HIV prevention programme, and assuring that his team would do everything to correct inaccurate information quickly: “First of all, some of the things I say will be incorrect and will have to be corrected; I mean, we will make mistakes, but we will act quickly to correct any error.”

a5726.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the US Department of Government Efficiency
a5726.speech: Said the number of condoms sent is high: “I am not sure we should be sending 50 million dollars in condoms anywhere, frankly; I am not sure it is something that would really excite Americans.” ; “That really is an enormous number of condoms. If it is for Mozambique rather than Gaza (the Gaza Strip), that is fine, it is not so bad. But still, why are we doing this?”

a5726.speaker: National Institute of Health (Mozambique)
a5726.speech: According to it, Mozambique has more than two million people living with HIV/AIDS.

a5726.speaker: CNN (investigation)
a5726.speech: A CNN investigation revealed that the agency did not spend that amount on condoms in the Middle East.

a5726.speaker: Provincial Health Services of Gaza province, Mozambique
a5726.speech: Contacted by STV, say that the province did not receive 50 million dollars' worth of condoms from the US and that the delivery of condoms to the province is not carried out directly by USAID.

a5834.speaker: G7 foreign ministers
a5834.speech: Reiterated their unwavering commitment to fostering peace, security, and stability in the Horn of Africa, particularly Somalia.

a5834.speaker: G7 nations
a5834.speech: Have pledged continued humanitarian assistance to those in the Horn of Africa who are grappling with food scarcity, poverty, violence, and the repercussions of severe weather and displacement.

a5834.speaker: G7 foreign ministers
a5834.speech: Voiced their apprehension over the Memorandum of Understanding signed between Ethiopia and the region of Somaliland in Somalia this past January. The G7 urges both the Ethiopian government and the Federal Government of Somalia to maintain open communication channels. They emphasize the importance of dialogue to avert further tensions, urging cooperation with regional allies, adherence to international law, and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, as outlined in the UN Charter.

a5834.speaker: G7 foreign ministers
a5834.speech: Commended Somalia for its significant strides in institutional building, economic management, and security reforms. They encouraged Somali authorities to persist in their efforts against Al Shabaab and to push forward with institutional development, including the completion of a transparent and inclusive constitutional reform.

a5834.speaker: G7 foreign ministers
a5834.speech: Highlighted the critical need to monitor the handover of security duties to Somali forces, with the mandate of the African Union Transitional Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) set to conclude at the end of 2024. They welcomed ongoing plans by Somalia and the African Union to establish a multinational mission to succeed ATMIS.

a5879.speaker: Advocates (HIV prevention experts)
a5879.speech: Have called for massive awareness campaigns in light of the recent approval of new HIV prevention technologies, noting limited knowledge among target groups.

a5879.speaker: United States Food and Drug Administration (US-FDA)
a5879.speech: Has indicated that Lenacapavir will be available at a low cost of $40 per person per year in 120 low and middle-income countries starting in 2027.

a5879.speaker: Elina Mwansinga, Executive Director of Y+ Global Malawi
a5879.speech: Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, said Lenacapavir is being introduced at a time awareness about Cab LA remains very low in Malawi and that some people thought it was a cure for HIV: "As such, there is a need for community awareness but we also need to capacitate our media houses to ensure that they can also escalate the information. We need orientation as well as training, especially on the key people who work with other large populations, to ensure that there is demand for these services. And we also, if we see that the quality is also not that good, we can also empower more people to advocate."

a5879.speaker: Elina Mwansinga, Executive Director of Y+ Global Malawi
a5879.speech: Noted that the new prevention tools are costly, and that Malawi should begin enhancing domestic health financing amid declining donor support.

a5879.speaker: Edna Tembo, Executive Director of the Coalition for Women Living with HIV
a5879.speech: Has said Malawi needs to be more proactive, as decision-making often takes too long: "We have always delayed in adopting new technologies, a problem exacerbated by bureaucratic tendencies."

a5879.speaker: Media Aids and Health Watch (statement)
a5879.speech: In a statement released yesterday, has bemoaned delays to raise awareness on HIV preventative measures, saying "lack of aggressive public awareness campaigns is making some people believe that HIV and Aids are no longer threats to Malawi. This perception is silently fuelling HIV infection cases."

a5879.speaker: National Aids Commission (report)
a5879.speech: A recent report indicates that Malawi successfully achieved the global 95-95-95 targets by 2024, ahead of the 2025 deadline.

a5974.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia 2024 Annual Report
a5974.speech: Delivers a warning that cannot be ignored: the country's commercial banking sector is in sustained and worsening decline. Between 2022 and 2024, four balance sheet indicators of a healthy banking sector - total assets, bank capital, deposits, and credit to the economy - posted back-to-back annual declines. The data shows that the downturn started in 2022 and 2023 during Weah's administration, but that the contraction deepened during the first year (2024) of President Boakai's administration.

a5974.speaker: Ambulah Mamey, International Development Practitioner (manages a portfolio of multi-sector USAID-funded resilience programs in Somalia, Tanzania, and Burundi)
a5974.speech: Told the New Dawn that the Central Bank of Liberia's 2024 Annual Report delivers a warning that cannot be ignored: the country's commercial banking sector is in sustained and worsening decline, and added that the numbers are not just discouraging, they reflect deep institutional vulnerabilities and policy inertia that now threaten the recovery agenda of the Boakai-Koung administration ; pointed out that commercial banks' total assets contracted from L$314.4 billion in 2022 to L$207.42 billion in 2024 - a staggering 34% drop; that bank capital fell from L$45.15 billion to L$31.44 billion, a 30% erosion in financial stability; that loans dropped from L$103.01 billion to L$76.6 billion, a 26% contraction; and that customer deposits plunged by 41%, from L$228.77 billion to L$135.56 billion ; observed that the drop in total bank assets between 2023 and 2024 amounted to L$86.5 billion, more than four times the decline posted for 2022 and 2023, and that deposits fell by L$63.15 billion under the Boakai administration - more than double the previous year's loss ; "The decline in credit under the Boakai administration (L$16.24 billion) surpassed the L$10.17 billion drop in 2023. This is the hidden collapse we can no longer ignore!"

a5974.speaker: Ambulah Mamey, International Development Practitioner
a5974.speech: Said the implications of the decline are profound: a shrinking banking sector undermines the government's ability to mobilize domestic capital, and it cripples access to credit for small and medium-sized enterprises ; "They impede poverty reduction, job creation, and inclusive growth; the core promises of the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID)," noting that the "AAID places private sector expansion at the heart of its economic strategy, but that ambition is incompatible with reality in the banking sector. It is clearly impossible for the current trend in the banking system to channel resources into the real economy as needed, but despite these signals, there is no policy response of sufficient scale or urgency."

a5974.speaker: General Auditing Commission audit of the Central Bank of Liberia
a5974.speech: Found widespread financial mismanagement and governance lapses and issued an adverse opinion - a rare and serious verdict in public sector financial auditing. The report cited "material weaknesses" affecting the Central Bank's operations and called for urgent executive and legislative action.

a5974.speaker: Ambulah Mamey, International Development Practitioner
a5974.speech: Explained that this moment could have marked a turning point, but that instead of using the audit as a launchpad for reform, the administration backed away from accountability; governors of the bank implicated in mismanagement were rewarded with hundreds of thousands of U.S. dollars in exit benefits while mid-managers who were used as agents of loots and corporate gangsterism remain with the bank.

a5974.speaker: Credible reports (unattributed)
a5974.speech: Credible reports suggest that the reward decision was influenced by actors close to the presidency who traded personal financial gain for accountability; reinforcing the idea that many policy makers in Liberia are more tolerant of failure than committed to accountability and reform.

a5974.speaker: Ambulah Mamey, International Development Practitioner
a5974.speech: Explained that it is not too late to reverse the course but doing so will require bold, coordinated action from both the Central Bank and the Ministry of Finance; said regulatory reforms must be enforced to ensure compliance with capital adequacy, risk controls, and governance standards, adding that even more urgently, public trust must be rebuilt and confidence in the banking system restored ; said a credible response must prioritize restoring the functionality and attractiveness of the banking system to micro, small and medium sized (MSME) businesses in the real economy, which could include rolling out a credit stimulus facility to de-risk lending to MSMEs through strategic partnerships among the Central Bank, the Ministry of Finance, and commercial banks ; said the government must invest in expanding digital banking infrastructure and modernizing transaction systems; that a national banking literacy campaign should be launched targeting entrepreneurs and informal sector actors; and that the government must anchor these initiatives with safeguards that prevent elite capture ; said Liberia cannot achieve inclusive growth while its banking system is declining, stressing the decline is not a seasonal downturn but a result of structural deterioration and institutional inaction ; concluded: "The Central Bank must return to its core mandate of safeguarding monetary and financial stability, and the executive must lead with the courage to replace, penalize, and reform where necessary. The cost of continued inaction is already visible: falling investor confidence, reduced access to credit, rising unemployment, and deepening poverty. While the Boakai-Koung administration still has tools at its disposal - and the time to use them - the window is closing fast, and the lack of policy response of sufficient scale or urgency leaves much to be desired."

a6060.speaker: Donald Trump, outgoing US President
a6060.speech: was quick to proclaim himself the winner, before being contradicted by the figures coming out of the ballot boxes after the count in the key states.

a6060.speaker: American media, led by pro-Trump Fox News
a6060.speech: announced the news, which travelled around the world.

a6060.speaker: Joe Biden, US President-elect
a6060.speech: drew on his many years of experience to present himself as a unifier at each of his appearances and to promise to be the president of all Americans.

a6060.speaker: Joe Biden, US President-elect
a6060.speech: announced during his campaign that he would bring his country back into the Paris climate accords; his position in favour of the Iran nuclear deal is also known, unlike his predecessor who denounced it on arriving in power; he remains opposed to the rapprochement between Donald Trump and the North Korean regime and to the construction of a wall between his country and Mexico; on immigration, he is committed to abolishing the “Travel ban”, the travel restrictions affecting nationals of Sudan, Nigeria and Somalia.

a6060.speaker: Joe Biden’s campaign team
a6060.speech: promised relations of mutual respect with Africa.

a6215.speaker: President Filipe Nyusi and the British High Commissioner in Maputo
a6215.speech: Confirmed in May of this year, during the Mozambique Energy and Mining Conference and Exhibition, that construction of the Namaacha Wind Power Plant would commence; at the time, the only reported obstacle was the need to finalize certain details.

a6215.speaker: Samir Salé, Director of Development and Business at GLOBELEQ
a6215.speech: Assured earlier this year that the project was in its final stages, indicating that construction could begin between the second and third quarters of this year: “We are in the final stages of development and expect to begin construction in the second half of this year. We hope the President of the Republic will lay the first stone for the project. Our goal is to start construction during President Nyusi’s term,” said Samir Salé in an interview with AIM in May of this year.

a6215.speaker: Sources close to the company (anonymous)
a6215.speech: Have confirmed that the start of construction has been delayed.

a6215.speaker: GLOBELEQ
a6215.speech: According to GLOBELEQ, this will be the country’s first large-scale wind power plant, designed to produce 120 MW.

a6336.speaker: Importers in Addis Abeba
a6336.speech: Importers claim their banks demand to know how long their cash would idle before signing off on letters of credit. The message, they say, is clear: try the parallel market. ; Importers claim that deposit requirements often run at 150pc to 200pc, and approvals stretch from weeks to months.

a6336.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) mid-July review
a6336.speech: The IMF's mid-July review pegged the official-parallel spread at 15pc, blaming high transaction costs, thin interbank liquidity and the Central Bank's 2.5pc commission on bank-to-bank trades. ; IMF data showed that reserves reached more than three billion dollars, equivalent to about 2.1 months of imports.

a6336.speaker: Official data (bank foreign-currency supply figures)
a6336.speech: Official data reveal an uneven picture: Awash Bank provided 125 million dollars in July, 110 million planned in August; Dashen Bank supplied 112.6 million in July; Bank of Abyssinia 94 million (July–early August); Wegagen over 70 million; Bunna 47.7 million; and Sidama Bank made one million dollars available in July, while it slated four million for August.

a6336.speaker: Mamo Mehiretu, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6336.speech: Countered that the Central Bank's position is stronger, with reserves tripled in a year, and that auctions will continue, although he did not disclose the reserve amount.

a6336.speaker: Executives in private banks
a6336.speech: Blame rising remittance-transfer fees and self-regulated foreign exchange bureaus whose quotes allegedly drive up informal rates.

a6446.speaker: Judicial Court of Sofala Province (indictment)
a6446.speech: Accuses Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries Roberto Mito Albino of committing an environmental crime, for having ordered the illegal cutting of timber in Chemba district, Sofala province, an offence whose sentencing range runs from 12 to 16 years.

a6446.speaker: District Public Prosecutor's Office in Chemba (indictment)
a6446.speech: Confirms that the individual named Roberto Mito Albino does in fact hold the provisional DUAT, but that in the case file he presents no timber exploitation licence ; according to the indictment, in February 2024 Roberto Albino requested the services of EcoFarm Mocambique, Lda, for the clearing of 50 hectares out of a total of 500 hectares of his property.

a6446.speaker: District Prosecutor's Office of Chemba
a6446.speech: Declared that it had not managed to locate Roberto Mito Albino in order to notify him.

a6446.speaker: Ecofarm Mocambique, Lda (letter contesting the fine)
a6446.speech: Contested the penalty, arguing that the fine should be applied to the owner of the concession, in this case Roberto Albino, and not to the company that merely provided the tools for the clearing.

a6446.speaker: Centro de Integridade Publica (CIP) investigation
a6446.speech: “Ecofarm acknowledges, in the same letter, that Dr. Albino should have obtained the cutting and clearing licence within his concession,” the investigation states.

a6446.speaker: The defendants (arguidos in the case)
a6446.speech: Accepted that they had committed criminal offences, but defend themselves on the grounds that they did so because they were contacted by Roberto Mito Albino, through his intermediary, Xadreque Muanza, at the time the provincial delegate of the Zambezi Valley Development Agency (AdZ) in Sofala province.

a6446.speaker: Court clerk of Chemba (narrative certificate)
a6446.speech: Communicates to the District Prosecutor's Office that on 3 June 2024 he complied with all legal formalities, issuing a notification to Roberto Mito Albino and contacting him by telephone on his two numbers, but without success: “…it was not possible to notify the above-mentioned citizen by telephone because the person I contacted (…) said he did not know the above-mentioned citizen and that there had been a mistake in the number.”

a6446.speaker: Candido Patrocinio Zeca, director of the SDAE of Chemba
a6446.speech: Requested the postponement of the trial to 29 July or later, justifying the request by alleging health reasons combined with a lack of money to cover transport and accommodation expenses in the city of Beira.

a6446.speaker: James Anthony White, manager of TCT – Florestal Industrial (defendant)
a6446.speech: Also stated in a letter that he would be unable to be present at the trial.

a6446.speaker: Centro de Integridade Publica (CIP)
a6446.speech: Finds the act strange and speaks of possible reprisals: “Candido Patrocinio Zeca is today, in his capacity as district director of the SDAE, a subordinate of Roberto Mito Albino, now Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries, which may create not only discomfort and fear of testifying against his hierarchical superior, but also fear of reprisals after the trial. For when Candido led the case, in defence of the State, in February 2024, Roberto Mito Albino was director general of the Zambezi Development Agency and not a minister.”

a6483.speaker: World Health Organization
a6483.speech: Identified 30 countries as having a high burden of TB and HIV co-infections, 22 of which are located in sub-Saharan Africa.

a6496.speaker: Human Rights Watch (HRW) (press statement)
a6496.speech: To justify its concerns, the NGO pointed in a statement to “Trump’s record of rights abuses during his first term”, highlighting “his embrace of white supremacist supporters and ideology”; criticised the “anti-democratic and extreme anti-rights policies proposed by think tanks led by former [Trump] advisers and the campaign promises, including that of rounding up and deporting millions of immigrants and retaliating against political opponents”; recalled the record it compiled of the “rights violations” during the first Trump administration between 2017 and 2021, such as the “policies and efforts to expel asylum seekers and separate families at the US-Mexico border” or “fuelling a violent insurrection to overturn the results of a democratic election”; added criticism of Trump’s praise for “autocrats such as Viktor Orbán, Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong-un”; stressed that “the threat of abuse of executive power is all the more worrying because of a recent decision of the US Supreme Court granting presidents broad immunity from criminal prosecution for official acts carried out in office”; noted that although Trump denied any link to Project 2025, which “details many other abusive policies”, “many of his statements reflect premises” of that document, and censured his defence of “extreme policies” on migration such as “mass” detention or deportation; warned of a “growing threat” to the “right to abortion” given Trump’s “insistence” that “states should have the power to block access to basic health care”, causing “preventable deaths” and the criminalisation of private decisions; censured possible retaliation against “political enemies” and the suggestion of invoking the Insurrection Act to “mobilise the US armed forces and national guard” against protesters; and noted how Trump did not confront “repressive governments” and how he opposed environmental progress at the United Nations and the funding of humanitarian aid.

a6496.speaker: Tirana Hassan, executive director of Human Rights Watch
a6496.speech: “Rights-respecting institutions and officials need to hold the line during the Trump administration,” she argued, quoted in the statement.

a6496.speaker: Donald Trump, US president-elect
a6496.speech: Claimed victory in Tuesday’s presidential election: “I want to thank the American people for the extraordinary honour of being elected your 47th President,” he told supporters at the Palm Beach Convention Center in Florida.

a6554.speaker: Notice distributed to USAID staff early Monday
a6554.speech: Staffers at the U.S. Agency for International Development have been instructed to stay out of the agency's Washington headquarters ; Those still able to access the system received emails stating that the headquarters building would be closed to agency personnel on Monday, Feb. 3.

a6554.speaker: Elon Musk
a6554.speech: Announced that Donald Trump had agreed with him to shut the agency down.

a6554.speaker: Musk, Trump, and some Republican lawmakers
a6554.speech: Have accused it [USAID] of promoting liberal causes.

a6554.speaker: USAID staffers
a6554.speech: Say that approximately 600 employees were locked out of the agency's computer systems overnight.

a6554.speaker: Democratic lawmakers
a6554.speech: Have protested these developments, arguing that Trump lacks the constitutional authority to shut down USAID without congressional approval.

a6593.speaker: Manyathela Kheleli, Standard Lesotho Bank's Brand and Marketing Manager for Communications and Sponsorships
a6593.speech: "This symposium is about more than just connecting our local businesses to international markets; it's about equipping them with the necessary tools to succeed and thrive." ; "We are committed to making sourcing from the world's manufacturing hub easier for our businesses, allowing them to lower expenses and reach their full potential." ; "With the right resources and backing, there are no limits to what Basotho entrepreneurs can achieve." ; "We are transforming potential into real opportunities for the businesses that are vital to Lesotho's economy."

a6593.speaker: Attendees of the symposium
a6593.speech: Expressed enthusiasm and optimism about the prospects of direct sourcing from China, noting their eyes had been opened to the possibilities of importing directly, connecting to manufacturers and reducing costs.

a6596.speaker: Malawi Government
a6596.speech: Assured the citizenry that “all HIV/AIDS services will continue to be provided normally in all the public and private health facilities across the country”.

a6596.speaker: Dr. Samson Mndolo, Secretary for Health of Malawi
a6596.speech: Reacting to concerns from some sections of the society, including those living with HIV, on the uncertainty of availability of antiretroviral (ARV) following the health policy shift by the United States of America Government, said the country has adequate quantities of ARVs, test kits and other supplies ; “Further, the Ministry has put measures in place to secure more supplies and will be making updates accordingly. The ministry is advising the public not to panic as it will continue working around the clock, to prevent any stock outs of the necessary commodities.”

a6596.speaker: Concerned citizens living with HIV (open letter addressed to President Lazarus Chakwera)
a6596.speech: Published an open letter, addressed to President Lazarus Chakwera, among others demanding a public statement, outlining the immediate steps his government is taking to ensure that ARVs are available.

a6753.speaker: Bret Baier, Fox News anchor
a6753.speech: Asked Felix Tshisekedi, the president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, how his government would balance continued ties with the United States, including the negotiation of a critical minerals deal, with its deepening relationship with China.

a6753.speaker: Felix Tshisekedi, President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
a6753.speech: Responded that China's influence is not so much "waxing" in Africa as America's influence is "waning" ; pointed out that the DRC would be "very happy" to see a renewed US commercial presence there.

a6753.speaker: Vera Songwe, nonresident senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, and Witney Schneidman, nonresident senior fellow at the Brookings Institution (commentary)
a6753.speech: Write that while China's presence is perceived as increasingly prominent, the United States' influence has seen a downturn; that as of 2023 China's trade with Africa surpasses US trade by more than fourfold, a dramatic shift from 2000, when the US held the title of Africa's largest trading partner; and that with Trump's tariffs, the shuttering of USAID and the Millennium Challenge Corporation, the closure of Voice of America and the lapse of PEPFAR, America's footprint in Africa is shrinking fast, arguing that African countries should insist that critical-minerals agreements include value-added production on the continent.

a6753.speaker: Gallup poll published last year
a6753.speech: Showed that, for the first time, China's approval rating in Africa (58pc) had surpassed that of the US (56pc).

a6753.speaker: Studies (cited)
a6753.speech: Have shown that trade with the US increases value-added production, labour productivity, and labour demand in Africa.

a6753.speaker: African trade ministers
a6753.speech: Have agreed to fast-track policies that will promote trade within the continent, as well as diversify exports to reduce their countries' dependence on particular foreign markets.

a6816.speaker: Dr Mohammad Dauod Altaf, WHO Sudan Health Emergency Lead
a6816.speech: “Stabilization centres are a lifeline to more than 100 000 children who are severely acutely malnourished and suffer from medical complications. Keeping these centres open and running is a high priority for WHO,” said Dr Mohammad Dauod Altaf. “Our dedicated staff are on the ground, in the communities and in the stabilization centres, to support these centres.”

a6816.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a6816.speech: WHO continues to provide technical assistance and expert advice as well as critically needed supplies for the treatment of SAM with medical complications. “We use every available avenue to get supplies to wherever they are needed, but insecurity and bureaucratic obstacles continue to affect the timely distribution of life-saving medicines and medical supplies.” WHO states it is able to support the life-saving operations of stabilization centres since the start of the war thanks to the generous financial assistance of the Italian Development Cooperation, Japan and the United States Agency for International Development’s Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance.

a6816.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) projection
a6816.speech: If the situation does not improve, it is projected that in Darfur alone, 200 000 children will suffer from life-threatening hunger in 2024.

a6867.speaker: Kariakoo Markets Corporation (Shirika la Masoko Kariakoo)
a6867.speech: issued its list showing that out of 1,861 traders, only 819 were found to meet the criteria for returning to the market.

a6867.speaker: Hadija Shomari, one of the traders
a6867.speech: said she believes those decisions will do justice, because even she, despite being a leader of her area, had her name cut.

a6867.speaker: Sheila Mfinanga, trader
a6867.speech: said the issue of the increased fee charges is not a problem for them, because the main thing was first to get a space, since they would be ready even to take a loan as long as they are certain of doing business.

a6867.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a6867.speech: said the leaders of the traders' association should sit together with the market management to work out how they will carry out that exercise, while knowing that the market is due to be opened next month by President Samia Suluhu Hassan ; “So I ask you, in this verification we are going to conduct again here, there is a team from the PCCB, National Security, the Police Force and other investigative bodies, which are government organs. So for anyone who dares to bring trickery, let me tell you, everyone will carry his own cross.”

a6867.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a6867.speech: told the traders that, along with this verification being done, they should know that the fees they used to pay previously are not the ones they will pay now when they return to the market, because the market has been improved.

a6867.speaker: Traders at Kariakoo market
a6867.speech: said that involving their leaders was what they had wanted from the beginning, but unfortunately they were ignored.

a6867.speaker: Minja Msuya, Chairman of Dogo market
a6867.speech: said that had this cooperation been done from the start, the challenges that arose would not have existed.

a6867.speaker: Minja Msuya, Chairman of Dogo market
a6867.speech: said the verification will not take even three days because they all know each other, and explained that they believe the market's opening time next month will not be affected by that verification exercise.

a6898.speaker: Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) (statement)
a6898.speech: Commended the Lagos State Government for making significant strides towards funding critical water infrastructure across the state, particularly the Adiyan II Water Treatment Plant; said the steady progress on the project—12 years in the making—demonstrates that state-led and funded solutions remain the best pathway to expanding public water supply and achieving universal access to clean, safe, and affordable water for Lagosians.

a6898.speaker: Reports from Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s recent visit to the facility
a6898.speech: According to reports from Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s recent visit to the facility, Adiyan II is now 80% complete and remains on track for its 2027 completion timeline.

a6898.speaker: Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) (statement)
a6898.speech: Urged the state not to hand over Lagos’ water sector to private profiteers once these projects are completed; emphasised that privatising Lagos’ water supply would undermine the massive investments already made by the state ; ‘We strongly urge the Lagos State Government to resist any temptation to privatise or concession the Adiyan II project and other water treatment facilities across the state. Water is not a commodity to be sold to the highest bidder.
