If Adiyan II or any other public water facility is handed over to private corporations, Lagosians will suffer—higher tariffs, restricted access, and corporate exploitation,’ the nongovernmental organisation warned ; Cited failed privatisation experiments across Africa, where foreign-backed water projects collapsed due to skyrocketing costs, contract failures, and profit-driven policies that left millions without access to clean water ; Pointed to the recent withdrawal of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) from Lagos’ water sector as a critical lesson.

a6898.speaker: Akinbode Oluwafemi, CAPPA’s Executive Director
a6898.speech: “What is happening with USAID is a textbook example of why governments should never outsource critical infrastructure to external financiers with hidden agendas. The Lagos State Government must recognise this as a blessing in disguise and take full control of its water sector rather than leaving it vulnerable to shifting donor priorities, where financial commitments are subject to geopolitical agendas, austerity measures, and changing domestic policies in donor countries, all of which can leave both governments and communities stranded.”

a6898.speaker: Engr. Mukthar Tijjani, Managing Director, Lagos Water Corporation
a6898.speech: Has confirmed that the state is now seeking funding from other international agencies, including the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and France’s Agence Française de Développement (AFD), to sustain water infrastructure projects ; In an interview on this matter acknowledged, ‘…we need to rely on the state government more… it is more predictable…’

a6898.speaker: Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA)
a6898.speech: Raised the alarm about this development, warning that these financial institutions have a long history of imposing harsh commercial conditions on public utilities ; “JICA and AFD have a track record of attaching dangerous conditions to their loans and grants—cost-recovery tariffs, bulk water purchase agreements, and privatisation clauses and mandates that prioritise corporate profits over public welfare. AFD, in particular, has close ties to Suez, a corporation notorious for its aggressive pro-privatisation stance and the devastation it leaves in its wake. If Lagos aligns itself with these buccaneers, residents will soon be burdened with unaffordable water tariffs while the state loses control over its own infrastructure,” CAPPA cautioned.

a6898.speaker: Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) (statement)
a6898.speech: Encouraged Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu to not be discouraged with the withdrawal of USAID but to rather treat it as a blessing in disguise and make history by keeping Lagos’ water under full public control ; “This is a defining moment. Lagos has the opportunity to lead Africa’s water justice cause by rejecting privatisation and strengthening its public water systems… The state must invest in the Lagos Water Corporation and the Ministry of Environment and Water Resources, to enhance their operational efficiency, and ensure transparency in the sector rather than handing over control to foreign profiteers. The decisions made today will determine whether water remains a public good accessible to all Lagosians, or whether it becomes a luxury available only to those who can afford it” ; Urged Lagosians to remain vigilant and demand that their government prioritise people over profit.

a6934.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6934.speech: Has said the freezing of US aid will have a massive negative effect on least developed countries such as Malawi, especially on service delivery and ability to manage foreign exchange: "Malawi generates about $1 billion [about K1.7 trillion] annually when we require about $3.2 billion [K5.1 trillion]. With the freezing of US support there will be a huge gap in foreign exchange resources. This in turn will have a massive negative effect on the economy if we don't practise financial prudence."

a6934.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6934.speech: Called for mindset change so that Malawi can embrace socioeconomic growth and be self-reliant, and called on authorities to fight corruption and stabilise the economy before the situation gets out of hand.

a6934.speaker: US Department of State (data)
a6934.speech: According to the US Department of State, the US Government was giving more than $350 million (about K612 billion) to Malawi annually - equivalent to more than 13 percent of the country's 2024-25 National Budget.

a6978.speaker: Agence France Presse (AFP) and Radio France Internationale (RFI) (dispatch)
a6978.speech: According to a dispatch from AFP and RFI, the autonomous port of Cotonou has been conceded to Bollore.

a6978.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique of 7 August)
a6978.speech: Confirms that the Beninese government awarded Bollore the concession of a two-quay terminal at the port of Cotonou ; recalled that the construction of a new container terminal comprising two berths is part of a programme of reforms aimed at improving the performance of the Port of Cotonou, and that granting the concession to a private operator is an option made in the Convention signed with the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) ; in approving the communication, gave instructions to the Minister of State in charge of Foresight, the Minister of Economy and Finance and the Minister Delegate in charge of the Maritime Economy to have the Technical Denationalisation Commission notify the provisional award to the said group and to diligently finalise and sign the concession convention with the BOLLORE and SMTC Group.

a6978.speaker: Joseph Atti-Mama, Director General of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou
a6978.speech: Clearly indicated during an appearance on RFI's news bulletins that, under the MCA programme, Bollore was only to build two quays for the port.

a6978.speaker: Technical Commission (with MCA and MCC representatives and World Bank assistance)
a6978.speech: Proposed to declare the BOLLORE and SMTC Group the successful bidder for the project to grant a concession for the south container terminal at the Port of Cotonou.

a6978.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique of 7 August)
a6978.speech: Adopted several draft decrees, notably the draft decree on the revaluation of pensions paid by the National Social Security Fund (CNSS) following the revaluation of graded salaries and the raising of the Guaranteed Interprofessional Minimum Wage (SMIG), and two draft decrees creating Central Police Commissariats at Abomey-Calavi and Bohicon ; examined and approved reports by the Minister of Labour and the Civil Service on the 2nd ECOWAS Conference of Ministers of Labour and Employment and by the Minister of Administrative and Institutional Reform on the 47th session of the CAFRAD Board of Directors.

a6978.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique of 7 August)
a6978.speech: Noted, on examining the file on bonuses and allowances in the Civil Service, that there currently exist 44 various bonuses and allowances against 16 regularly provided for by Law No. 86-013 of 26 February 1986; that the current allowance system rests on no rational criterion and is "discriminatory, opaque, arbitrary, inequitable, disparate, irrational, heavy and complex to manage" and a source of untimely demands and strikes; and that accumulated bonuses received by certain State Agents far exceed their basic salaries ; said the Government is determined to carry out a profound reform, decided to entrust the study of the remuneration system to a consultancy firm with results to be submitted before 31 December 2009, stated that apart from the exceptional motivation bonus no other measure will be taken before validation of the study, and said the permanent dialogue engaged with the Trade Union Organisations will be maintained.

a6978.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique of 7 August)
a6978.speech: Authorised Benin's participation in the investiture ceremony of the re-elected President of the Republic of Congo in Brazzaville on 14 August 2009, and the organisation in Cotonou on 13 and 14 August 2009 of the annual Conference on deconcentration.
